failures.criterion: scripts/dispatch/README.md's Lexeme database procedure, the second and the concurrent run: running the setup block again must not break a server it already started.
failures.evidence: With the server from the first run still up in $TMPDIR/pg, a second run of the same block (bash -c 'source <block>') re-extracts the tarball over server/ in place. The live server's shared libraries are overwritten under it: the output was 'initdb: error: program "postgres" is needed by initdb but was not found', 'pg_ctl: another server might be running; trying to start server anyway', '/legion/scratch/tmp/t717r2/pg/server/bin/postgres: error while loading shared libraries: /legion/scratch/tmp/t717r2/pg/server/lib/liblzma.so.5: file too short'. Then psql -h $TMPDIR/pg -U postgres -Atc 'select 1' failed: 'server closed the connection unexpectedly'. Afterwards, ps listed no postgres process from that directory: the first server was dead, and the directory held a half-written server/. The old pgserver command (get_server) reused a running server, so a rerun was safe before this change. In this deployment $TMPDIR is /legion/scratch/tmp, which every role of an issue pod shares, so two roles that follow the README at the same time hit this. No red test: the defect is in README prose, and a test that reads source text is forbidden here. Reproduce: run the block, then run it again in a second shell. A fix: make the block start the existing cluster and skip the download, extraction and initdb when "$pg/data" already exists, or refuse with a message when pg_ctl status reports a running server.
